title: Thread Stack Isolation & Independent Execution Paths
prompt: Imagine Thread A currently executes function1() and Thread B executes function2(). Why can't they use the same stack?

forbidden_misconceptions: threads only need registers without stacks
evaluator_rubric.scoring_criteria: Learner must explain that the stack stores activation records (local variables, frame pointers, and return addresses). If threads shared a single stack, pushing and popping frames from independent functions would corrupt return addresses and overwrite each other's local variables.
evaluator_rubric.ideal_response_summary: Each thread executes its own sequence of function calls independently. The stack stores activation frames containing local variables and return addresses. If two threads shared a stack, Thread B pushing a frame for function2() would overwrite or interleave with Thread A's function1() frame, corrupting stack pointers, local variable offsets, and return addresses upon function exit.
